# mediaflow - INVARIANTS (generated from docs/requirements.toml; do not edit)

Normative, safety-critical subset of SPEC v1.0. Re-read before every build step. If a feature conflicts with a rule here, the feature loses.

- **[SAF-1]** Originals are moved to trash, never deleted; trash shrinks only by retention expiry or an explicit trash purge. There is no automatic early purge.
- **[SAF-2]** Publish only after every check passes: output opens; output duration is within max(1 s, 0.1%) of source duration and the video presentation tail (the maximum packet pts + duration) matches output container duration within the same tolerance; exactly one video stream and the planned stream counts; the planned video codec matches (the encoder family for an encode, the copied source codec for a remux) and every HEVC stream in an MP4 output carries the hvc1 tag; resolution, pixel format, SAR and frame rate match; every colour property the source states is present and equal in the output, while an unstated property creates no requirement; every planned audio track matches codec, channel count, channel layout, language and default disposition; every planned subtitle track matches codec, language, forced and default disposition; total bitrate >= min_output_kbps; the bits-per-pixel-per-frame floor (REVIEW) with its frame-count basis reported; full decode test. On failure the job is FAILED and the original untouched.
- **[SAF-3]** The final folder is staged in work/ on the library filesystem and published with one atomic no-replace rename into movies/. The verified output is moved into the staged folder; no output hard link or byte copy is used. inbox, convert, work, review, failed, trash and movies must share one st_dev or the daemon refuses to run. Every move is therefore a single rename.
- **[SAF-4]** An existing destination causes REVIEW duplicate. Only review accept --replace records an intent, moves the old library folder to trash with its own manifest, and then publishes. Nothing in movies/ is deleted or modified in place.
- **[SAF-5]** One deletion function only removes paths strictly under _pipeline/work, _pipeline/trash, or a job scratch directory; it refuses symlinks and paths with fewer than four components and logs every removal. One retire_move function moves into trash and never deletes. No shell=True or ad-hoc rm -rf.
- **[SAF-6]** Every step is idempotent and resumable. Start-up recovery handles encoding or earlier, adopts a published destination only when its marker and output hash match, adopts a retire already in trash, and completes replace and restore intents. SIGKILL is tested in every window plus a chaos loop.
- **[SAF-7]** One daemon holds flock on /run/mediaflow/daemon.lock; one encode runs at a time. Mutating CLI commands are queued for the daemon or executed by the CLI while holding the same lock.
- **[SAF-8]** Free space must be at least max(1.2 * source_size, min_free_gb) before encode and before publish; at publish the only additive reservation is the size of text sidecars staged with the output, because the output itself is moved on one filesystem. During encode, the watchdog pauses unless free space covers the bounded net remaining-work estimate plus an additive min_free_gb / 2 emergency reserve; bytes already written are not subtracted twice. Root and DB filesystems need root_min_free_gb. Trash counts and pauses above max_trash_gb. Trash is never purged early.
- **[SAF-9]** Layered protection: systemd limits, start gates (Jellyfin viewers, AC power, start temperature, schedule) and a coarse thermal SIGSTOP/SIGCONT stop last. The sensor is discovered by hwmon name; no sensor fails closed unless temp_sensor=none. Never touch fan or PROCHOT settings.
- **[SAF-10]** Run as mediaflow, never root, with no sudo. TMDb token is read from tmdb.env and sent only as an Authorization Bearer header, never in a URL. The notify URL is read only from notify.env. Both are redacted everywhere.
- **[SAF-11]** Fresh installs start with dry_run = true. Turning it off is explicit and logged. In dry-run no file is moved, renamed, or published.
- **[SAF-12]** A job goes FAILED with its original preserved after max_restarts. A stall detector kills a live, unpaused encode with no progress for stall_minutes and counts a restart. An ffmpeg version change pauses the queue until capability tests pass.
- **[SAF-13]** Every ffmpeg and ffprobe call includes -protocol_whitelist file,crypto,data. The probed container must be in the format allowlist. Only regular files are processed; symlinks inside preset folders are ignored and reported.
- **[SAF-14]** Calibration measures the production operation: the same planner, command builder, encoder, backend and target geometry as an encode, over an explicitly requested source interval. It never substitutes a backend silently; without an eligible backend it refuses and names the reason. The quality reference is the same source interval, decoded and scaled to the planned geometry, so both sides cover the same frames; a failed comparison or a frame-count mismatch is reported as not available with a reason, never as a number. A trial is seeded into the speed table only when it is valid, and the seed is keyed by the backend that actually ran.
- **[SUP-1]** Production verification streams video-packet and decoded-frame scans with memory bounded independently of the number of records. It sums video packet bytes, keeps packet count distinct from decoded-frame count, and derives the presentation end from the maximum packet pts + duration rather than the last packet in file order. A cancelled or interrupted scan returns no partial result.
- **[SUP-2]** Cancellation or a protection termination wins over a late worker result; partial hashes and scans are discarded. Every owned child process is terminated and reaped, and the exclusive expensive-operation slot and job scratch remain owned until a non-cooperative worker has actually exited.
- **[SUP-3]** Success, failure, cancellation, stall, overall timeout, protection interruption and deferral are distinct outcomes. Only uninterrupted success may publish output or seed a speed-table value. A controlled encode interruption caused by protection or daemon shutdown preserves the original, discards the partial output and is recovered at PLANNED without consuming a restart; an encode stall, encode timeout or genuinely interrupted encode consumes one. A verification interruption never advances the job to VERIFIED.
- **[STATE-1]** Every job state, review reason, intent kind, command status and transition belongs to one shared vocabulary. Active, terminal, resumable, review and user-visible classifications are derived from it. Database queries generate SQL placeholders from the shared sets; no module maintains its own state tuple. Adding an unclassified state fails tests and import validation. RESTORED is terminal for scanning and queueing but remains visible in status history, listings and retention.
- **[CONFIG-1]** Every configuration key has one reload classification: live, future-jobs, restart-required or rejected. Reload validates the complete config, presets and secrets before atomically publishing one generation. Restart-required keys retain their old effective values and remain visibly pending until restart; invalid reloads keep the previous generation and clear only the invalid-config hold. An active operation keeps its effective policy until the next safe boundary. Plans record the configuration generation and preset fingerprint; stale plans re-plan deliberately without consuming a restart.
- **[COMPAT-1]** The database schema version is enforced. Older databases are backed up, then migrated by ordered, idempotent, transactional steps; newer databases are refused without modification. Semantic generations are explicit in plans, speed rows and capability files: pre-state-colour plans re-plan, legacy speed rows are retained but not reused, and unversioned capability files are unknown. Job history is never discarded, and restore preserves the previous database.
- **[DEPLOY-1]** Every unverified hardware or deployment claim has one registry item with a class, runner, exact procedure, expected result, failure interpretation, risk, evidence path and status. The generated markdown view is fresh, and only recorded on-box evidence may mark an item verified-on-hardware. The agent never marks an on-box item verified.
- **[DEPLOY-2]** Doctor reports pass, fail and unknown outcomes separately for required, feature-conditional and informational checks. It exits non-zero only for required failures or enabled feature failures, never writes to media or state, never migrates the database, never performs network checks, and routes every subprocess through bounded supervision. Unknown is never reported as pass or as a failure of the tested capability.
- **[DEPLOY-3]** Installer and upgrade logic is rehearsed against a fake root: fresh install, repeat, over an older install, partial failure and refusal on a newer schema. Existing config, secrets and state are preserved. Evidence bundles record revision, timestamp and redacted command output without titles or secrets, and the registry updater accepts only complete, consistent bundles.
- **[DEPLOY-4]** Host-only installation must not create or change media roots, enable services or timers, or change pre-existing service states. Runtime startup and scanning must not create, chmod or chown library paths. Observational CLI commands must not create or migrate databases. The initial workflow and automatic ffmpeg-change retests must never invoke software/x265 capability probes; hardware-only checks are explicitly requested separately, and skipped or incomplete probes stay unknown.
- **[SCHED-1]** A job starts only when its estimate fits before the window closes; once started it may overrun. A job that can never fit stays queued with paused reason estimate-exceeds-window, is reported once by status, and notifies after 30 minutes. run --force is the only override.
- **[REV-1]** Every REVIEW reason records its origin state and resumes at the state in the review table. Clearing a review never skips planning, encoding, or verification.
- **[MP4-1]** Every HEVC video stream in an MP4 output (encode, remux, already-efficient and not-smaller fallbacks) gets -tag:v hvc1 and -movflags +faststart.
- **[MP4-2]** Video may be stream-copied into MP4 only when it is H.264 or HEVC. A remux to MP4 from another codec goes to REVIEW with reason remux-incompatible-video.
- **[MP4-4]** Normalise language tags, drop commentary and audio-description tracks when exclude_commentary is true, prefer languages (original means default track language or first audio track), apply unknown_language, then fall back to the default or first audio track with a warning. Never produce zero audio if the source had audio. Default track first, then source order, up to max_tracks.
- **[MP4-6]** Bitmap subtitles (PGS, VobSub/dvd_subtitle, DVB) cannot go in MP4. With mkv_fallback, output the title as MKV with subtitles copied and record container mkv (bitmap subs). With drop, discard them and record it in the manifest.
- **[MP4-10]** HDR10, HLG and Dolby Vision sources go to REVIEW with reason hdr unless the preset has hdr = keep. A keep remux copies the stream. A keep encode needs ten_bit_source = keep and working 10-bit encode. Never silently tone-map.
- **[MP4-11]** Interlaced sources go to REVIEW and are cleared by moving to a remux preset or rejecting.
- **[MP4-12]** Stream selection uses one explicit -map for each chosen stream and never -map 0.
- **[SIZE-2]** If encoded video stream bytes exceed in_video_bytes * (1 - min_savings_pct/100), discard the encode and re-plan as remux at plan_version + 1 with fallback_from = encode, reusing the audio and subtitle selection. If remux is incompatible the job goes to REVIEW. Recovery honours the recorded plan version.
- **[SIZE-3]** Never publish an encode whose video stream is larger than the source video; it follows the SIZE-2 fallback. Remux jobs are exempt from must-be-smaller.
- **[SIZE-4]** Never upscale. Keep the source frame rate (VFR stays VFR) and preserve display aspect ratio and SAR.
